articles.title: Constantine Director 'Hopeful' for Sequel After DC Studios Shakeup
articles.summary: The director of Constantine, Francis Lawrence, opened up about the movie's long-awaited sequel now that DC Studios has had a changing of the guard.
body: James Gunn and Peter Safran are out at DC Studios in a sudden and unexpected move that has sparked no end of worry and speculation among fans. Gunn, for his part, cited a distaste for the “corporate” side of the job, but confirmed that projects already in motion, like Man of Tomorrow, are still a-go.

Fans aren’t the only ones scratching their heads about what might happen next. Francis Lawrence, the director of oodles of Hollywood blockbusters, is also in this boat — though he’s rather optimistic about the situation, as it means he might finally get the chance to make another Constantine film.

Speaking with Collider ahead of his next movie, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, Lawrence clarified that he isn’t happy for anyone to lose their jobs, but admitted that he’s keen on the possibility of getting Constantine 2 off the ground now that things are changing at DC.

articles.title: Monster Hunter Outlanders Review
articles.summary: This mobile spin-off maintains the gameplay loop and visuals of its console counterparts, with the caveat of how progress gates push microtransactions.
body: My biggest surprise with Outlanders is how uncompromising the scope of its world feels, right in line with a big mainline Monster Hunter, supported by the fact that this game looks absolutely stunning, and runs like a dream. On an iPhone 14 Plus I was able to run the game on High settings with a stable 45fps, and almost zero slowdown, even during intense battles.

The actual act of exploring the world feels just as entrancing as in major Monster Hunters. Various options for constructing camps and equipment as you explore the world make both traversal and item gathering easier. Camps unlock fast travel points and places to rest, catapults send your adventurer flying on their glider at high speed, and resource collectors constantly soak up those valuable items you need.
points: This mobile spin-off maintains the gameplay loop and visuals of its console counterparts, with the caveat of how progress gates push microtransactions.

articles.title: Queen’s Domain Review: The Perfect Skyrim Replacement for Right Now
articles.summary: I love Skyrim. I love returning to the spine-tingling haze of ’90s first-person games like Doom, Quake, and Myst. But what I really love is a modern game that feels like a lost relic from that era, not a nostalgic imitation but something that might have actually existed.
body: Queen’s Domain pulls off that illusion spectacularly, embracing the creepy, low-polygon aesthetic of FromSoftware’s King’s Field while building something far more ambitious. Instead of just paying homage to the cult-classic RPG series, it feels like a lost installment, unearthed decades later and somehow better than I could have imagined.

Queen’s Domain requires no prior knowledge of King’s Field, but for those completely in the dark about FromSoft’s history, the studio’s games have never been walks in the park. The danger is real, the stakes feel high, and Queen’s Domain immediately wallops anyone who thinks they have a handle on how to navigate the “easy” creepy-crawlers littering the opening patches of grass. You are truly at level 0 when you wash ashore on the mysterious Isle of Neasied, and the few surviving soldiers you meet early on will be devoured before lending much help.

articles.title: The 2026 LEGO Star Wars Advent Calendar Is Discounted at Target After Amazon Sells Out
articles.summary: This year's lineup of LEGO Advent Calendars have started going out of stock ahead of Black Friday. Unsurprisingly, the Star Wars-themed calendar is one of the first to have completely disappeared from major retailers.
body: If you've been hoping to pick up the 2026 version of this calendar, this is probably your last chance to do so at a discount. Here's a quick rundown of where you can still find this set in stock online.

Target isn't the only retailer that still has stock available, but it is by far the best deal you'll find online right now. Both Barnes & Noble and Macy's are great places to check for stock after a LEGO set disappears from all other shelves, but it's pretty rare to find discounts on such sets there. Once Target officially sells out of its own inventory, those are the next best places to shop if you want to avoid paying a mark-up.

This year's LEGO Star Wars Advent Calendar is themed after The Mandalorian and Grogu movie, featuring minifigures of The Mandalorian, Grogu, Moff Gideon, Carson Teva, and a Jawa. Most of these characters are also dressed in festive sweaters. You'll also get to build miniature versions of Mando's N-1 Starfighter, The Razor Crest, a Sandcrawler, and more. The set comes with a total of 293 pieces, which is actually 30 more than what we got with the 2025 edition.

articles.title: Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra Is Reportedly 'Close to Done,' Though at the Cost of Cutting Back on Content and Length
articles.summary: Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, Amy Hennig's Captain America/Black Panther game, is reportedly close to being finished, but it could be extremely compromised. According to a new report from Kotaku, Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra is "close to done." The news comes hours after rumors began spread online that…
body: Kotaku's report went on to describe the game's development as difficult, which should come as no surprise to anyone who's been following its journey. The title was announced in 2024 and has been delayed several times, with little to no news or footage beyond that.

Kotaku claims that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra initially began as a Netflix game, but was later expanded for consoles and PC. Unfortunately, the title is reportedly "light on gameplay," with most of the action mapped to one button and the experience lacking "significant interactivity."

The project has also allegedly gone well over budget, and as a result, has had to "significantly" scale back from its original vision in terms of content and length. As of right now, we have no idea when Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra will release, but if it really is nearing the finish line, we could see something next year. Unfortunately, it doesn't seem like the game will be a hyper-engaging action/adventure title with riveting action, from the sound of it.

articles.title: Steam’s Growing Review Backlog Has Cost Another Game Its Launch Date
articles.summary: Steam's growing backlog for approving game builds appears to be getting worse, as yet another studio's game is stuck in the purgatory of the platform's review program.
body: "Unfortunately, we're stuck waiting for Steam to review and approve our launch build. We have been waiting for a few weeks now and sadly don't know when they will finally get around to it," Australia Did It publisher Mystic Forge wrote in an update. "We're hoping to be able to launch as soon as possible and will update all of you the second we get an update. We really appreciate all of your continued support and apologize for the situation. We can't wait for you to check out the final game and hope to be able to get it into your hands soon!"

Australia Did It co-developer and game designer Rami Ismail said the game was originally submitted on October 20, and a minor controller issue caused it to fail. That bug was fixed the same day, but since then, Ismail and Aesthecian Labs have been stuck waiting for Steam approval.

articles.title: Netflix's Hit Spy Thriller Returns and Takes Over Streaming Charts
articles.summary: Keira Knightley has a knack for playing smart, determined women who refuse to back down when things get dangerous. Whether she's exposing government secrets in Official Secrets, investigating a serial killer in Boston Strangler, or navigating a deadly mystery aboard a luxury yacht in Netflix's The…
body: Now, she's back in the spy business with a returning Netflix series that's attracting plenty of streaming attention.

The second season of Black Doves arrived on Nov. 5, and the spy thriller wasted little time climbing Netflix's charts. The series reached No. 2 on the global Netflix TV chart, according FlixPatrol. Netflix's own weekly figures also show that season 2 of Black Doves attracted 3.8 million views between Nov. 2 and Nov. 8, making it the fourth most-watched English-language series of the week.

Black Doves follows Helen Webb (Knightley), a seemingly ordinary politician's wife and mother who is secretly working as a spy for a clandestine organization called the Black Doves. For a decade, she has been passing along her husband's political secrets to the organization while maintaining her carefully constructed family life.

articles.title: Destroy All Humans remake developer goes independent, splits from THQ Nordic and parent company Embracer Group
articles.summary: Black Forest Games - the studio that remade the first two cult-classic Destroy All Humans games - has spun out from under former owners THQ Nordic and Embracer Group.
body: The Destroy All Humans remaker won its newfound independence through a management buyout, and wasted no time at all in co-founding Third Signal, which is described as a new group of independent studios that'll eventually provide help and resources to other indie teams.

"Some of the best games of the last decade came from teams of 50, not 500. Black Forest Games is one of them, and the right studio to launch Third Signal. Our vision is to build a developer driven group and give teams the independence, resources and creative freedom to continue their creative legacy and bring their own ideas to life," Third Signal CEO Andreas Tobler said in a press release.

Black Forest Games was one of Embracer Group's earliest high-profile acquisitions almost a decade ago, before the company swallowed up countless big names (Lord of the Rings, Tomb Raider, Kingdom Come: Deliverance, more) in the following years and spat back a bunch shortly after. Most infamously, Embracer sold Gearbox and Borderlands during its massive internal restructuring in 2024.

articles.title: Don't expect more information on The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel "for some time," Bethesda says
articles.summary: After Bethesda formally named The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel earlier this month, some series fans were hopeful that more news wasn't far behind. Skyrim is 15 years old today (11th November) after all, but Bethesda Game Studios has since dashed those hopes into oblivion.
body: In response to a Reddit post speculating about possible Sentinel news on Skyrim's birthday, the official Bethesda Game Studios account chimed in to temper everybody's expectations.

"Hey everyone, wanted to pop in to say that we aren't going to have any big announcements tomorrow," the social media account wrote. "We're excited you're excited but we will not be sharing anything new on Sentinel for some time."

The Elder Scrolls fans have already been waiting for the series' next mainline follow-up for, erm, also quite some time. Specifically, Skyrim came out in 2011, The Elder Scrolls 6's first reveal trailer reared its head in 2018, and BGS' Starfield took to the stars in 2023 - a wait so long that it had even the most faithful among us questioning if a new Elder Scrolls could ever recapture the series' magic.

So, there you have it - don't expect to see or hear about Sentinel anytime soon. Better yet, lock it up in some corner of your brain and be pleasantly surprised when it does miraculously reappear in 20XX.

articles.title: CD Projekt used AI to modify the voice of Geralt's Polish actor after a stroke left it significantly changed: 'This was a special case'
articles.summary: Jacek Rozenek was the voice of Geralt in all previous Polish-language Witcher releases, and CD Projekt wanted to work with him again—but his voice is no longer a match.
body: Game File reports that CD Projekt worked with AI company Respeecher to modify the voice of Geralt's Polish voice actor in the upcoming Songs of the Past expansion for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt.

The actor, Jacek Rozenek, voiced Geralt in the Polish editions of all the Witcher games, including The Witcher 3 and its two expansions, and the Game File report says his performances are highly regarded. But in 2019, he had a stroke that left him temporarily unable to speak; by 2021 he had rehabilitated enough to be able to provide some new lines for The Witcher 3's next-gen update, but the process left him "exhausted."

Still, he continued to train and was eventually able to return to work, and when CD Projekt decided to make a new Witcher 3 expansion it wanted him back for the role. But the stroke, and the passage of time, had left Rozenek's voice noticeably changed. Given that Songs of the Past will occur in the midst of The Witcher 3, that shift in tone—"lower [and] gruffer," according to Game File's Stephen Totilo—presented a problem.

articles.title: GTA 6 might be censored in Japan, if the game's smaller install size and lack of "strong sexual content" warning is anything to go by
articles.summary: GTA 6 is finally coming out worldwide next week, putting an end to a 13-year wait and at least one popular meme format, but the highly-anticipated game might look a bit different in Japan.
body: Now that pre-loading is live for the Rockstar Games mammoth, players across the globe can finally download the game and drool over its icon for the next week or so. But pre-orderers in Japan have noticed that GTA 6's file size comes to about 208GB on the PlayStation and Microsoft Stores, versus up to 212GB in other regions.

As reported on by GameSpark and covered by Automaton, the game also received the strictest age rating from the Japanese certification board CERO - "Z" which is recommended for players aged 18 and over - but the listing notably doesn't contain one disclaimer seen in other international ratings.

PEGI and ESRB both warn of the game's "strong sexual content." Curiously, CERO's rating includes no such disclaimer. Together, some fans have taken the lack of "sexual content" disclaimer and smaller file size as signs that GTA 6 might not include some of the risque content we know it'll flaunt elsewhere in the world - based on NSFW leaks and a past rating that already clued us into the fact GTA 6 might be the first GTA to feature full-on sex scenes.

body: Black Forest Games, German developer of early Kickstarter success Giana Sisters: Twisted Dreams, as well as remakes of the first two Destroy All Humans games, and, er, Bubsy: The Woolies Strike Back, has announced it's leaving THQ Nordic after nine years within the Embracer Group subsidiary.

Following a management buyout, Black Forest has founded an indie studio group called Third Signal. "Some of the best games of the last decade came from teams of fifty, not five hundred," said Third Signal's founder and CEO Andreas Tobler. "Black Forest Games is one of them, and the right studio to launch Third Signal. Our vision is to build a developer-driven group and give teams the independence, resources and creative freedom to continue their creative legacy and bring their own ideas to life."
